name: Minimal cell
oneLine: The simplest known free-living cell, built in a lab in 2016.
howItWorks: It runs one loop: take in food, make energy, build parts, copy DNA, split. Every part you have met so far is inside. Remove one and the loop breaks.
deeper: JCVI-syn3.0 was made by stripping a bacterium’s genome down to 473 genes (Hutchison et al., 2016). It divides about every three hours.
sizeComparison: a 250th the width of a hair
simplification: We show a few hundred molecules. The real cell holds millions.
